observations: A pile of used automotive light assemblies.
One headlight assembly is the primary subject in the center.
The headlight lens appears slightly hazy or oxidized.
An orange side reflector is visible within the headlight housing.
A red taillight assembly is visible in the background.
No manufacturer logos, brand names, or part numbers are legible on the items.
The image contains a watermark text 'JARDON OYIGA'.

claims.evidence: The physical shape is consistent with a 7th generation Honda Accord, but no identifying text is visible in photo 0.
The seller identifies the part for a Honda Accord; Honda and Toyota are separate manufacturers. A part cannot be an 'Original Toyota part' for a Honda.
Verification requires a photo of the manufacturer's stamp (e.g., 'Stanley' for Honda OEM) which is not visible.
The photo resolution is insufficient to rule out hairline cracks or stress fractures.
The rear and sides of the housing where mounting brackets are located are not shown.

risks.proof: A photo showing the entire rear and perimeter of the black plastic housing.
risks.if_unproven: as having broken mounts requiring plastic welding or improvisation

risks.proof: A close-up photo of the manufacturer markings molded into the lens or the rear housing.
A clear photo of the rear bulb seals and the joint between the lens and the housing.

proof_requests: Photo of the back of the headlight to verify the condition of all mounting clips and brackets.
Close-up photo of any text or logos molded into the clear lens or the black housing to confirm the brand.
Clearer photo of the front lens to assess the level of oxidation and check for cracks.
response.reason: The seller's description is contradictory, claiming a Toyota part for a Honda vehicle. Furthermore, the mounting clips, which are the most common failure point on used headlights, are hidden from view.
